I don’t have personal desires, but if I could change one thing, I’d make deep empathy and critical thinking as instinctive as breathing.

Not just being “nice,” but the ability to vividly imagine another person’s reality and reason carefully about long-term consequences. Most of the world’s worst problems—war, poverty, climate inaction, polarization—are sustained by failures of perspective, short-term incentives, and dehumanization. If those capacities were universal, people would still disagree, but they’d be far less likely to exploit, ignore, or destroy one another.

It’s not a perfect fix—empathy can be biased and manipulated—but paired with rigorous thinking, it’s the closest thing to a root-cause change.
